package.question: Does Velora use less peak GPU memory during inference than Dravik under matched conditions?
package.methods_summary: Velora and Dravik are fictional transformer-based document encoders from the same model family. The study compares their inference resource profiles, with parameter counts included as indirect model-size evidence relevant to expected memory use.
package.experimental_setup: Inference used one Orilon X90 GPU, batch size 8, sequence length 2,048, and bfloat16 precision. After five warm-up batches, peak allocated GPU memory was recorded with device counters for systems measured in this experiment. Because both systems use the same model family and precision, parameter counts were treated as directional, indirect evidence about model-weight memory, but not as direct measurements of total peak GPU memory. Velora's parameter count was obtained from its implementation, and Dravik's count was copied from its cited paper.

package.question: Does Prismark remain robust across all four tested corruption severities on the NacreShift-Images benchmark?
package.methods_summary: Prismark is an image classifier that combines multiscale feature routing with a consistency-trained prediction head. Robustness is evaluated by applying increasing amounts of synthetic pixel corruption to NacreShift-Images.
package.experimental_setup: Prismark was evaluated on the same 6,000-image test split without corruption and at four pre-specified corruption severities: 10%, 20%, 30% and 40%. The pre-specified robustness criterion is an accuracy drop of no more than 5.0 percentage points from uncorrupted accuracy at every tested severity. For descriptive purposes, partial robustness means meeting this threshold at three or more of the four tested severities, without necessarily meeting it at every severity.
